title: A 17-slope bank with midpoint noise scaling loses signal recovery in GW150914 data
abstract: A 17-slope drift bank tests a measured gap in an earlier GW150914 tone search. We search 40-500 Hz and -0.2 to +0.2 Hz/s at 2-18 seconds after merger. Midpoint noise scaling gives target ranks 0.656 and 0.783. No candidate passes the threshold. At detector hrss 1e-22 strain sqrt(s), the bank recovers 0/94 signals at each of three slopes; a paired tone test recovers 94, 25 and 42. Removing 329-334 Hz from the loudest bank calibration block reduces its score from 946 to 82. A synthetic narrow line gains a score factor of 462. These checks show a noise-scaling failure in this record. They do not identify a line source or test a repaired search. Small tail samples, one injection frequency, equal amplitudes and a hardware-injection flag limit the result. Code, aggregate evidence, source hashes and retrieval steps are supplied. Raw strain stays external.

display.caption: The bank has a larger noise floor and no recovery at the shown amplitude. Error bars are conditional exact 95 percent count intervals.

citations.reason: We test its drift gap with the same raw data, interval and control design.
Earlier pulse search and instrumental-line warning.
